reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 12 and targeted source-note crop, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native note/right-edge crop, full white/cyan/alpha sheet and evidence, and unchanged naiwa.png; checked frontal cap portrait, separated cap emblems, absence of facial hair, uniform, collar, backing, and source note rows/right tab against returned additions and omissions.

remaining_reasons: The source's small dark right-edge note tab is absent from the returned note's plain right edge. Restore the original compact dark tab and its edge position/form without adding different hardware.

The returned native note has two main upper gray-mark rows plus an additional isolated lower-left gray dot below them. The enlarged original has only the two compact upper rows and no such third mark. Remove the invented isolated dot and restore only the source-scale two-row upper footprint and spacing.
entries.positive_observation: The dark navy peaked cap retains a glossy black visor, gold cord/piping, one small upper gold emblem and one separate lower pale circular wreath/cockade. Covered hair, dark brows, no glasses, no moustache or beard and one stern closed mouth remain. The strictly frontal upright pose, direct gaze, crop and pronounced visor shadow are retained. The dark navy jacket keeps gold shoulder accents, white pointed shirt collar and dark tie; the rounded chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk or pinching. The complete dark frame and opaque muted olive-grey photographic backplate remain. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte ring. These correct portrait and compositing properties do not offset the clear note-tab loss and added gray dot.
entries.visible_limitations: Internal cap-badge detail, small gold shoulder ornament and note lettering are not reliably readable at 65x67 and are not rejection grounds. The native return clearly resolves the missing tab and separate extra dot, while the enlarged source shows their original absence/presence; no glyph transcription is required.
